name: Erik Abbott

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a usual shift look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and have traced parcel complaints at a contact centre for nine years. I finished secondary school and handle the usual disputes at about the same speed as the rest of the floor. The longer service has lifted my pay above many agents here. I keep a paper callback sheet and have never used AI tools.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife runs the counter at a garden shop. We have two school-age children, eight and twelve, a mortgage and eight months of expenses saved. Several other centres are nearby. I want an account record and a named person when a parcel goes missing, not a guess from a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the afternoon team the new shortcut is fine if someone checks the customer record. A parcel marked delivered to the wrong door still needs a person to trace it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have done this work for nine years and my pay has risen with service, so I expect my shift to hold. We have eight months of expenses saved, although a mortgage and two children make that money a reserve rather than spending cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the parcel complaint calls and the paper handover sheet that tells the next shift who owns a callback. In the first year I'll replace what we took from savings for the car repair before paying for another holiday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about my job. I prefer knowing the route a parcel took to trying another screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who shares the house costs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wife runs the front counter at a garden shop, and our children are eight and twelve. Her wages and mine cover the house, but we built the reserve in case one stopped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the suggestion box?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I have never used the AI suggestion box. If a new button becomes compulsory, I want written instructions and a practice account before it touches a customer's parcel.

say: I'd accept a **small shortcut** after a human checks the record.
I'd keep a **person tracing parcels** sent to the wrong door.
think: I expect my **experienced shift** to hold in a mild change.
Our **eight-month reserve** protects a mortgage and two children, rather than funding treats.
do: Keep handling **parcel complaints** and recording named callbacks on my paper handover sheet.
Restore **car-repair savings** before another family holiday in the first year.
feel: **Calm** about a familiar job and secure household reserve.
S0.quote: A parcel marked delivered to the wrong door still needs a person to trace it.
fieldNote: His **nine years** explain higher pay without making him a team lead.
He has **never used AI**, preferring the parcel record and a named callback owner.
He treats **eight months saved** as mortgage protection.

steps.text: Keep taking parcel complaints and recording named callbacks on paper
Replace savings used for the car repair before booking another holiday

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the centre to show which paid shifts change before it hands delivery chats to software. I don't object to a tool that works, but a fast wrong answer creates another call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the simple tracking work that fills half my day could vanish. My higher wage and service record might make me costly to keep, even though several other centres are nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll ask for written figures on repeat parcel calls and keep my current shift. If the answer system becomes required, I'll practise with a supervisor on closed accounts during paid hours; in the first year, if my hours fall, I'll apply only for posted paid jobs whose written hours and wages cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the pay packet, not only the software. Eight months saved gives me time, but a small cut each week would slowly eat it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a safe tool test use?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take ten old parcel cases to the supervisor and compare the wrong addresses with the software's answer. I won't use a live customer's account as my first lesson.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check at another centre?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the other centre for its full weekly rota and hourly rate before giving notice. A higher title with fewer paid hours would leave us worse off.

say: I'd request **paid-shift plans** before delivery chats move.
I'd count **repeat parcel calls** when judging fast software replies.
think: I worry my **higher wage** may make my experienced post costly to keep.
do: Request **repeat-call figures** and stay on my shift this month.
Practise **required AI replies** only on closed accounts with paid supervision.
Apply after **actual hour cuts** only for posted paid work with written mortgage-covering wages and hours.
feel: **Anxious** about a smaller weekly pay packet.
S1.quote: A higher title with fewer paid hours would leave us worse off.
fieldNote: He separates **small weekly cuts** from a dramatic dismissal.
His **supervised practice** depends on the tool becoming required and paid time.
His **written rota** check protects the mortgage from a false promotion.

steps.text: Keep working the current parcel complaint shift while hours remain
Practise required AI replies on closed accounts with supervisor during paid hours
Apply after cuts only for posted paid work with written mortgage-covering wages and hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell colleagues full thinking AI by 2028 could answer our tracking calls, even the awkward ones. Robots around 2031 do not give a headset job three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my parcel role could end; the other local centres might be changing too. Eight months saved can buy a search, but my wife's garden-shop wage will not carry the mortgage and children alone indefinitely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'll ask for written notice dates and put our car-replacement plan on hold while the current car is safe. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I'll apply for a posted paid building-attendant role only if its hours and wages cover our bills; I won't pay for a course until a real vacancy requires it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, even with the reserve. A whole line of work can disappear faster than eight months feels on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your wife?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my wife what the centre has said in writing, not repeat a rumour at dinner. We would check the car first; if it becomes unsafe, we fix it before protecting any savings target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why consider building work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I helped maintain the community hall on weekends, but that was volunteer work. I'd ask the building manager what a full paid attendant shift actually includes, especially before hands-on robots arrive around 2031.

say: I'd warn **2028 AGI** could answer even difficult tracking calls.
I'd remind agents **2031 robots** do not extend headset work.
think: I expect my **parcel job** could end with nearby centres shrinking too.
I know **eight months saved** cannot replace my wage indefinitely.
do: Request **written notice** and delay car replacement only while the current car stays safe.
Apply for **posted paid attendant work** after a real cut only if hours and wages cover bills.
Check **required course fees** only after a real vacancy is posted.
feel: **Alarmed** by a field-wide loss despite a savings reserve.
S2.quote: Eight months saved can buy a search, but my wife's garden-shop wage will not carry the mortgage and children alone indefinitely.
fieldNote: His **reserve** cannot replace earnings across a contracting field.
The **car delay** ends if the vehicle becomes unsafe.
He knows **volunteer hall work** is not proof of a paid attendant wage.

steps.text: Delay replacing the car only while it remains safe to use
Apply for posted paid building-attendant work after a cut only if wages and hours cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years is time to find out which paid jobs really need people. Our calls face general AI in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could stay on parcel disputes while I inspect a building job. I won't call attendant work safe forever, but I might earn there before the robots change it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my current calls and ask the community hall about a supervised paid attendant day if a place is posted. If an employer posts a paid role with bill-covering wages and hours and funds its required safety class on paid time, I'll complete the class; in the first year after 2031 I'll move only on a written offer that still meets those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but able to test a workday before changing jobs. I want more than my memory of volunteer Saturdays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the workday show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want to see the early opening, cleaning and what the attendant does when a visitor falls. If the trial is unpaid, I won't call it a route to income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wife and I would check whether a new rota still lets us collect the children after school. A written wage is useful only if the hours work for our household.

say: I'd check **posted paid places** during the five-year window.
I'd separate **2031 call risk** from later 2034 robots.
think: I could **inspect attendant work** while keeping call wages.
I do not assume **hands-on work** remains safe after robots arrive.
do: Keep my **parcel calls** and request a supervised paid attendant day only if a place is posted.
Complete **funded safety class** on paid time only for a posted role with mortgage-covering wages and hours.
Move after 2031 only for a **written offer** with bill-covering wages, hours and workable school pickup.
feel: **Anxious**, though a paid trial could show the real work.
S3.quote: A written wage is useful only if the hours work for our household.
fieldNote: He wants **paid supervised trial** because volunteer work differs from a full shift.
His **class condition** includes a posted role, funded fees and paid time.
His **childcare test** applies even to a bill-covering written offer.

steps.text: Keep answering parcel calls while they pay
Complete funded safety class on paid time only for posted role with mortgage-covering wages and hours
Move only for written paid offer with bill-covering wages and hours fitting school pickup
Try supervised paid attendant day only if a place is posted; decline unpaid trials

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade lets a family compare actual offers without leaving work on a guess. General AI reaches calls in 2036, then hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 the children may need less care, but our mortgage may still be due. I'd rather protect the good wage I have and check building work slowly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my parcel shift and add part of each pay to our reserve. I'll inspect posted building-attendant work once a year; in the first year after 2036 I'll move only if my call hours fall and a written paid offer has stable hours, covers the mortgage and fits the school route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about a future change, steady about this month's income. A decade lets me be careful without ignoring the date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you build the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would like a full year of expenses saved, but only from wages we actually receive. If my current hours fall, the target moves back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the children to ask what a job pays for a full week, not only what the title sounds like. Our family budget lives on weekly hours.

say: I'd compare **written paid offers** during the decade, including the full week of hours behind each wage.
I'd distinguish **2036 calls** from robots around 2039.
think: I may still owe a **mortgage at 53**.
I prefer to keep **good current pay** while checking building work.
do: Keep my **parcel shift** while it pays well.
Save part of **actual wages** toward a full year of expenses.
Move after 2036 only after **call-hour cuts** and with written paid wages, stable hours and school pickup covered.
feel: **Uneasy** about the future, secure on present wages.
S4.quote: Our family budget lives on weekly hours.
fieldNote: His **one-year reserve target** takes longer if paid hours fall.
He keeps **current higher pay** rather than moving for a title.
The **school route** matters beside mortgage-covering wages.

steps.text: Keep handling paid parcel calls while full shifts remain
Save part of actual wages toward one year of expenses
Move after cuts only on written paid offer with stable hours covering mortgage and school pickup

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The parcel calls could vanish before a building job has a real opening, and nearby centres may cut together. Written notice and posted paid attendant work with mortgage-covering hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who takes a callback after a machine closes a parcel case. The customer still needs someone to check the address photo and give a real answer. A fast reply is not a delivered parcel.

headlineQuote: A fast reply is not a delivered parcel.
portrait: Erik is an **experienced 43-year-old agent** with secondary schooling and average skill on parcel complaints.
His **service pay** is higher, and the household has eight months saved, a mortgage and two school-age children.
He has **never used AI** and keeps paper handovers; many nearby centres offer alternatives if jobs stay open.
The **2028 date** alarms him; later timelines permit a funded paid trial of building work before hands-on robots arrive.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his parcel wage while nearby centres cut together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** would show when the income may stop.
A **posted paid attendant role** with stable mortgage-covering hours would offer a route.
